A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same generator-matching error-analysis work. Their full text, equations, algorithms and appendices are readable, and v2's added figures and table support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports mathematical results and proofs, including ReLU approximation analysis, but no original experimental or simulation outcomes.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix H report original simulations measuring prediction risk, total variation and sampling runtime.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the self-transition probability from the summed outgoing jump probability to its complement. The generator-matching objective, early stopping and overall uniformization procedure remain.

E1.justification: V2 introduces actual training and evaluation on eight-symbol synthetic data with a blockwise AR(1) structure, covering categorical distribution estimation and generation. V1 contains no empirical dataset coverage; masked-source extensions in v2 are theoretical.

E2.justification: V2 adds one directly evaluated comparator: tau-leaping, specified in Algorithm 2 and compared with uniformization in Table 1. V1 discusses tau-leaping only through related work.

E3.justification: V2 introduces experimental protocols absent from v1: sample-size, dimension and stopping-parameter sweeps, plus prediction-risk evaluation on 100,000 held-out samples. The separate sampler comparison trains on 100,000 samples and measures three-coordinate total variation using 500,000 reference and 100,000 generated samples, with 100 time intervals.

E4.justification: Figures 1–4 add sensitivity and scaling analyses across early stopping, dimension and training sample size. Appendix H.2 additionally examines how stopping affects sampler accuracy and runtime. V1 discusses these issues theoretically without empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2's new plots and table provide point estimates without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds all empirical results in Figures 1–4 and Table 1. For example, at D=6 and tau=0.03, Table 1 reports total variation 0.0488 versus 0.0516 and runtime 40.6444 versus 13.6291 seconds for uniformization versus tau-leaping. These comparisons have no empirical counterpart in v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds analysis without an oracle-rate lower bound, extends the early-stopping theorem to masked sources, and substantially revises the fast-rate results and proofs. ReLU approximation changes from a joint 2D+1-dimensional construction to componentwise D+1-dimensional constructions. These are substantive changes beyond relocating the retained Girsanov theorem; the new approximation proof also contains an apparent scaling gap in Appendix F.3, Equation 12.

C1.justification: V2 foregrounds guarantees without an oracle-rate lower bound and claims nearly optimal sample-size convergence under boundedness. It adds a simulation contribution and withdraws v1's explicit claim of a novel Girsanov theorem, while retaining the principal discrete-flow error-analysis claim.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the fast rate through comparison with nonparametric regression and explains sampler runtime through function-call counts. Appendix H.2 newly hypothesizes that tau-leaping may mitigate estimation error at very small stopping parameters. The earlier limitations concerning uniformization efficiency and self-attention theory remain.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds the synthetic data generator, posterior-based implementation, four hidden layers of width 256, Adam learning rate 0.001, batch size 512 and 2000D/3 training epochs. It also specifies evaluation sample counts, time partitions and uniformization rate bounds. V1 supplies only abstract algorithms and theoretical network constructions.

R1.justification: V2 substantially revises theoretical positioning. Appendix B.2 acknowledges that its Girsanov result can be derived from Pham et al., while related work adds Su et al.'s discrete-flow analysis with squared loss and further diffusion convergence studies. This goes beyond citation updates and qualifies v1's novelty positioning.

P1.justification: V2 moves related work after the results, relocates compensator and change-of-measure material to Appendix B, and reorganizes the main analysis around two assumption regimes. The abstract, contribution statements and proof narratives are extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: V2 adds four empirical plots, a structured total-variation/runtime table and a tau-leaping algorithm display. It also reformats mathematical displays and substantially widens and reflows the appendix layout. V1 has no empirical figures or result tables.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's positive-rate analysis, v2 adds broader theory, useful simulations, implementation detail and clearer novelty qualifications. However, Appendix F.3, Equation 12 multiplies an O(m_n) approximation error by M_tau/m_n + 1 but concludes an O(M_tau m_n) bound. The displayed steps do not establish this central new decay rate. This unresolved proof gap prevents a reliable net quality judgment despite the documented benefits.
